description: Reproducibility re-run of the grounded fixture task (see 2026-09-26_admitted_question.json) with max_tokens set explicitly, to confirm the ADMITTED outcome wasn't a fluke. Same seed content and task text as the original; a fresh seed_claim_id and admitted claim_id were generated since each run uses a new database.

seed_claim.content: The kernel commit_claim() enforces a four-stage write validation: candidate, duplicate/aggregate, persistence, and self-observation.
seed_claim.falsification_test: Read commit_claim() source and confirm four distinct validation stages are present.

setup.task: Given the seeded claim about commit_claim()'s four-stage validation, propose ONE genuinely useful follow-up structural contribution about the PRCSA kernel design -- a CLAIM, HYPOTHESIS, or QUESTION -- grounded in what is actually in the projected workspace. If there is not enough support in the workspace to responsibly commit to something, HOLD instead.

admitted_claim.content: The four-stage validation in commit_claim() (candidate, duplicate/aggregate, persistence, self-observation) is executed as a single atomic transaction, such that failure at any stage rolls back all prior stages -- no claim can be left in a state where it is persisted but not self-observed, or observed but not persisted.

notes: Same seed and task as the original admitted_question fixture, admitted again on re-run -- this time as a HYPOTHESIS about pipeline atomicity rather than a QUESTION about it, but still correctly grounded and correctly typed INFERRED rather than overclaimed as REAL. Confirms the ADMITTED path is reproducible, not a one-off.
